name: Salesforce Certified Platform Developer II (Plat-Dev-301)
retake: US$100 plus applicable taxes (50% of the registration fee)
prereq: An active Salesforce Certified Platform Developer (formerly Platform Developer I) credential
delivery: Booked through Trailhead Academy and delivered by Pearson VUE, either online proctored or at a test center (Webassessor/Kryterion delivery ended in July 2025). No hard-copy or online materials allowed during the exam.
maintenance: Complete one maintenance badge on Trailhead each year (the Platform Developer certification maintenance badge, e.g. Winter '26 due December 4, 2026); the credential expires if you miss the deadline.

sections.title: Advanced Developer Fundamentals
objectives: Understand the implications of using localization and multi-currency features and capabilities and how they affect coding.
Given a scenario, justify using sharing objects and Apex managed sharing.
Given a scenario, identify best practices for various types of custom metadata and custom settings, and how to implement required solutions.

sections.title: Process Automation, Logic, and Integration
objectives: Given a scenario, identify the considerations when multiple declarative and programmatic processes interact.
Given a scenario, determine an optimal programmatic or declarative solution.
Given a scenario, demonstrate the use of Apex trigger best practices.
Given a scenario, demonstrate error handling best practices and how to preserve transaction integrity.
Given a scenario, write advanced SOQL to query data.
Given a scenario, identify when and how to use asynchronous Apex (future, Queueable, Batch, Schedulable).
Given a scenario, identify the use cases for and demonstrate the use of dynamic Apex.
Given a scenario, identify the appropriate publish / subscribe logic for platform events.
Given a scenario, identify and implement the appropriate inbound and outbound integration techniques (REST/SOAP services, callouts, Named Credentials).

sections.title: User Interface
objectives: Given requirements and code snippets for a Lightning web component or Aura component and its Apex controller, identify the changes needed to meet the requirements.
Given a scenario, identify the Visualforce techniques for actions, partial page refreshes, and asynchronous processing.
Given a scenario, identify best practices for displaying errors in the user interface.
Given a set of requirements, choose the appropriate technology: Lightning Web Components, Aura components, or Visualforce.
Given a scenario, identify how to build responsive markup based on the form factor of the device.
Given a scenario, demonstrate event communication between Lightning web components and Aura components.
Explain the purpose of static resources and how they are used in Visualforce, Lightning Web Components, and Aura components.

sections.title: Testing, Debugging, and Deployment
objectives: Given a scenario, determine how to test Apex classes and triggers, including the use of mocks and stubs (HttpCalloutMock, Stub API, Test.startTest/stopTest, test data).
Given a scenario, identify how to test and debug Lightning web components, Aura components, Visualforce, and JavaScript (including Jest unit tests for LWC).
Given a scenario, determine why Apex code is not behaving as expected and how to debug it (debug logs, checkpoints, Apex Replay Debugger).
Given a scenario, formulate the deployment process, supporting tools, and mechanisms for source-driven development (Salesforce CLI, scratch orgs, packages, metadata/destructive changes).

sections.title: Performance
objectives: Identify common performance issues for user interfaces and the techniques to resolve them.
Given a scenario, choose the appropriate logic and query structure to maximize application performance and handle large data volumes (selective queries, indexes, Query Plan).
Given a scenario, analyze where performance gains can be made by using asynchronous callouts (e.g. Continuation).
Given a scenario, identify where code reuse is applicable and how it should be implemented.
Given a scenario, identify inefficiencies in sample code and demonstrate how to resolve them.

tips: Read the official exam guide first and weight study time by section: Process Automation, Logic, and Integration is 27% of the exam.
Work through the official Trailhead trailmix in a Developer Edition or Trailhead Playground org; hands-on practice beats reading.
Expect long scenario-based questions with code snippets; read the last line (what is being asked) before the code.
Multiple-select questions tell you how many answers to choose; all must be correct to score.
There is no penalty for guessing, so answer every question and flag uncertain ones for review.
Budget about 2 minutes per question (65 questions in 120 minutes) and leave 15 minutes to revisit flagged items.
Up to 5 unscored questions are mixed in; don't let an odd question rattle you.
Know the order of execution, async Apex limits, and selective-query rules cold; they recur across sections.
For online proctoring, run the Pearson VUE system test in advance, clear your desk, and use a wired connection if possible.
Arrive or check in early (online check-in opens before the appointment); bring a valid government-issued ID matching your registration name.
Questions align to a specific release noted in the guide; prefer documented platform behavior over very recent release features.
Schedule the exam date first; a fixed deadline keeps a 4-6 week plan on track.

tasks: Read the official exam guide end to end
Complete Company-Wide Org Settings (multi-currency, localization)
Build Apex managed sharing with a custom row cause
Complete Custom Metadata Types; compare with hierarchy/list custom settings
Study Triggers and Order of Execution; map flow/trigger interactions
Refactor a trigger into a handler framework with bulkification and recursion control
Practice savepoints, Database methods with allOrNone=false, and custom exceptions
Write advanced SOQL: aggregates, semi/anti-joins, polymorphic TYPEOF, FOR UPDATE
Complete Asynchronous Apex; chain Queueables and use Database.Stateful batches
Use Dynamic Apex: describes, dynamic SOQL with bind variables, user-mode security
Complete Platform Events Basics; publish from Apex and subscribe with trigger, flow and empApi
Complete Apex Integration Services with Named Credentials
Build an LWC calling Apex via @wire and imperatively, with error display
Practice LWC-to-Aura and child/parent event communication
Review Visualforce actionFunction, actionSupport, rerender and remoting
Use static resources and form-factor responsive markup
Write tests with HttpCalloutMock and the Stub API
Complete Unit Test Lightning Web Components (Jest)
Debug with debug logs, checkpoints and Apex Replay Debugger
Deploy via Salesforce CLI to a scratch org; review package vs org development models
Complete Large Data Volumes and read the LDV best practices doc
Use the Query Plan tool to evaluate selective vs non-selective filters
Implement a Continuation for a long-running callout
Take timed practice sets, revisit weakest section, and re-read the exam guide objectives
